correctness.rationale: Two exhaustive 15-edge face tests agree on 32768 cases; 331 nonempty simplices. The specified 159-pair discrete-Morse matching is proved acyclic by a 990-relation topological sort. Exact signed unit-pivot reductions yield a 7x7 Morse differential whose only independent rows have a determinant-minus-one minor, giving Smith factors (1,1). As its two-skeleton is a wedge of seven S^2, Hurewicz and integer elementary CW changes reduce the attaching maps to two cancellable pairs, proving a wedge of five S^2 and five S^3. Original simplicial ranks are independently verified modulo 2,3,5,7; such ranks by themselves are not an integral proof.

originality.rationale: Four relevant full manuscripts (two historic and two later) have been inspected at the material needed to determine their hypotheses, main theorems, and the explicit Petersen-name ambiguity; the original 1994 article was bibliographically verified but full journal text not accessible. Current public mathematical records and relevant archived claim statements were searched for the exact and equivalent objects. No inspected statement has the Petersen graph as underlying graph of the ordinary matching complex with this integral homotopy type. Indexed results concerning M_2(P), M(K_5) and the Petersen discrete Morse complex do not logically imply it. Residual unindexed and inaccessible-full-text priority risks remain; novelty is best-knowledge relative to inspected evidence, not proof of global priority.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph KG(5,2) is a canonical highly symmetric cubic graph, not an arbitrary parameter specialization. Its ordinary matching complex has nonpure maximal matchings of three sizes and nontrivial adjacent-dimensional homotopy, so its complete integral homotopy type is a motivated small finite invariant. The precise attaching information and torsion-free wedge are not supplied by Euler characteristic, single-field Betti counts, or the nearby non-Cohen–Macaulay criterion; they provide a reproducible reference example for comparing graph matching complexes with higher-matching and Morse complexes.
